name: Dawn at Ceres
keyDiscovery: Discovered that dwarf planet Ceres harbors extensive sodium carbonate salt deposits inside Occator Crater, revealing a subsurface briny ocean reservoir that erupted through cryovolcanism.
missionLegacy: The first spacecraft to orbit two different extraterrestrial destinations (Vesta and Ceres) using high-efficiency xenon ion propulsion; safely placed in an unpowered quarantine graveyard orbit for 50+ years.
funFact: Dawn traveled 6.9 billion kilometers powered by just 425 kg of xenon gas — its ion engines operated for over 51,000 hours, equivalent to nearly 6 full years of continuous thrust!
heritageNote: Dawn remains parked in an uncontrolled, ultra-stable graveyard orbit around dwarf planet Ceres, protected by planetary protection protocols to avoid contaminating potential cryo-habitats on the surface.

objects.name: Dawn Spacecraft
objects.description: Robotic explorer measuring 19.7 meters wing-to-wing. Carried three xenon ion thrusters, framing cameras, and a visible/infrared mapping spectrometer. Currently orbiting silently around Ceres in a perpetual graveyard orbit.
objects.whySent: To explore the two most massive protoplanets in the asteroid belt (Vesta and Ceres) and unlock the early chemical conditions of our infant solar system 4.5 billion years ago.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Proved that Ceres is an active, water-rich dwarf planet with an ancient global ocean, subsurface briny reservoirs, and organic molecules on its surface.
objects.ongoingScience: Even in graveyard orbit, Dawn's decadal datasets of gravity anomalies and spectral data continue to be re-analyzed by astrobiologists modeling deep extraterrestrial oceans.
objects.firstPerson: Listen up, space cadets! I am the Dawn Spacecraft, and I am the only probe in human history to orbit two different extraterrestrial bodies — asteroid Vesta and dwarf planet Ceres! Powered by futuristic ion thrusters, I traveled nearly 7 billion kilometers on a whisper of xenon gas. Ran out of hydrazine in 2018, but I am still orbiting Ceres in eternal silence. Solar system globetrotter, no cap!

objects.name: Cerealia Facula Salt Dome
objects.description: A dazzling 10-kilometer bright dome of sodium carbonate salts and ammonium chloride in the center of Occator Crater. Formed when subsurface brines erupted through cryovolcanic fractures caused by asteroid impact.
objects.source: Nature Geoscience (De Sanctis et al. 2020) / Dawn VIR Spectrometer
objects.whySent: To explain the mysterious brilliant white spots on Ceres that baffled astronomers upon Dawn's initial approach in 2015.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Confirmed the highest concentration of carbonate minerals ever detected outside Earth, proving active hydrothermal or cryovolcanic brine processes in dwarf planets.
objects.ongoingScience: Comparative planetology researchers use Cerealia Facula chemistry to model Europa and Enceladus ice plume compositions.
objects.firstPerson: Earth telescopes thought I was an alien beacon! I am Cerealia Facula — the gleaming white spot in Occator Crater on Ceres. Dawn flew down to just 35 kilometers to snap my portrait, proving I am made of sodium carbonate salts left behind by ancient cryovolcanic brines erupting from an alien subsurface ocean. I glow like a disco ball on a dwarf planet!

objects.name: GRaND Gamma-Ray Detector
objects.description: Gamma Ray and Neutron Detector mounted on Dawn. Measured elemental concentrations of hydrogen, iron, potassium, and carbon by analyzing cosmic-ray-induced gamma emissions from the top meter of regolith.
objects.whySent: To map global subsurface water-ice distribution and elemental abundance across Ceres' entire crust without touching the surface.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Discovered that water ice makes up roughly 10% to 30% of Ceres' upper regolith by weight, proving Ceres is a giant ice-rock world rather than a dead dry asteroid.
objects.ongoingScience: Data actively constrains solar system formation models and where water ice condensed in the early solar nebula.
objects.firstPerson: I see through solid alien rock using cosmic rays! I am the Gamma Ray and Neutron Detector, or GRaND, on Dawn. By counting neutrons kicked up by galactic cosmic rays, I mapped the subsurface water-ice hidden across Ceres — ten percent water by weight! I have got x-ray vision for solar system geology, pure superhero vibes!

objects.name: NSTAR Xenon Ion Engine
objects.description: Triple electrostatic 30-centimeter ion thruster package using xenon propellant ionized by electron bombardment and accelerated through 1,280-volt molybdenum grids.
objects.source: JPL Ion Propulsion Technical Report / Brophy et al.
objects.whySent: To demonstrate that high-specific-impulse electric propulsion can enable complex multi-body orbital rendezvous missions that conventional chemical rockets cannot achieve.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Validated ion propulsion efficiency in deep space with an Isp of 3,100 seconds — roughly 10 times higher efficiency than standard chemical rocket engines.
objects.ongoingScience: Paved the way for modern electric propulsion architectures on missions like NASA's Psyche, DART, and Gateway lunar outpost.
objects.firstPerson: Who needs explosive rocket fuel when you have sci-fi blue plasma? I am Dawn's NSTAR Ion Thruster! I shot charged xenon ions out the back at 90,000 kilometers per hour, accelerating non-stop for over two thousand days using less fuel than a family minivan. The ultimate endurance runner of deep space, built completely different!
